skill.name: checkpoint
skill.description: Save coding session progress to memory-keeper so task state, modified files, blockers, and next steps can be recovered.
skill.summary: Create progress checkpoints for coding sessions before context loss or compaction.

security_audit.summary: All static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline code spans in SKILL.md. I found no prompt-injection text, shell execution, network exfiltration, or executable script content. The main residual concern is low-severity persistence of project progress data to memory-keeper.

remediation.suggestion: Add user guidance to exclude secrets, customer data, and confidential file names before saving checkpoints.

remediation.issue: Memory-keeper examples are unlabeled Markdown code fences.
remediation.suggestion: Mark examples as text and clarify that they are memory-keeper tool calls, not shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Checkpoint Data Persistence Includes Project Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs saving task descriptions, modified file lists, blockers, next actions, and todo state to memory-keeper. This is the advertised function, but it can persist sensitive project metadata if users include confidential details.

content.value_statement: Long coding sessions can lose progress when context ends. This skill records task state, changed files, blockers, and next steps for recovery.
actual_capabilities: Captures the current task, changed files, progress state, blockers, and next action.
Saves progress items with memory-keeper keys and priorities.
Creates a named checkpoint with a timestamp-based label.
Prepares compaction when the active context becomes large.
Provides a short confirmation summary after saving a checkpoint.
limitations: Requires a compatible memory-keeper tool to store checkpoints.
Does not recover state by itself; recovery depends on a separate recovery workflow.
May persist sensitive project context if users include secrets in tasks or todos.
Does not verify that file lists or progress estimates are complete.

use_cases.title: Preserve Long Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Save task state after significant coding progress so work can resume after context loss.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Context Compaction
use_cases.description: Capture key progress details before reducing or replacing the active conversation context.

use_cases.title: Create Debugging Handoffs
use_cases.description: Record tested hypotheses, blockers, and next steps during multi-step troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Save a Basic Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use checkpoint to save my current task, changed files, progress, blockers, and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Checkpoint Before a Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Before I refactor the auth flow, create a checkpoint with current progress and rollback notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Context Compaction
prompt_templates.prompt: My context is getting large. Use checkpoint to save progress, prepare compaction, and list what I should do after recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Detailed Handoff Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current session state, identify missing context, save a named checkpoint, and produce a concise handoff summary.

output_examples.input: Use checkpoint after finishing the settings page.
output_examples.output: Checkpoint saved for settings page work. It records completed UI changes, modified files, remaining validation tasks, and the next test run.

output: Progress saved with high-priority task and next-action entries.
A named checkpoint was created for recovery.

output_examples.output: Checkpoint saved with the current bug, tested hypotheses, active blocker, touched files, and the next diagnostic step.

best_practices: Checkpoint after each completed file or major test run.
Review checkpoint content before saving confidential tasks or file names.
Keep next-action notes specific enough for immediate recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not store API keys, credentials, or private customer data in checkpoint text.
Do not rely on checkpointing as a replacement for version control.
Do not create checkpoints with vague progress or missing next steps.

faq.question: Does this skill run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The file contains Markdown examples for memory-keeper tool calls, not shell execution.

faq.question: What tool does it require?
faq.answer: It requires a memory-keeper-compatible context saving tool.

faq.question: Can it restore lost context?
faq.answer: It saves recovery data, but restoration depends on a separate recovery command or workflow.

faq.question: Is it useful for Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents compatible workflow steps for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I save secrets in checkpoints?
faq.answer: No. Keep credentials, tokens, and customer data out of checkpoint text.

faq.question: How often should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after significant changes, before compaction, and before ending long sessions.
